message.content:
In Blackjack, an **Ace** is a special card because it can count as **either 1 or 11 points**, depending on which value gives the best advantage to the hand without causing a bust.

### How it works

| Situation | Ace’s value |
|-----------|-------------|
| If counting the Ace as 11 keeps the total ≤ 21 | 11 |
| If counting the Ace as 11 would make the total > 21 | 1 |
| If you have two Aces | One Ace is usually counted as 11 and the other as 1 (so the pair totals 12). |

### Why this matters

- **Flexibility**: The Ace gives you a “soft” hand (e.g., Ace‑7 = 18) that can still improve if you draw another card.
- **Avoiding bust**: If you already have a high total, the Ace automatically switches to 1 to keep you in play.

So, the rule is simple: **an Ace is worth 11 unless that would bust your hand, in which case it’s worth 1.**
